_meta: A grayscale image's intensity histogram, described as two overlapping populations of pixels: a dark background and a brighter foreground object. Each cluster is {mean, std, weight} over the 0..255 intensity range; the code builds the normalized histogram from them deterministically (a discrete Gaussian per cluster, summed and normalized -- no sampling). true_fg_fraction is the real fraction of foreground pixels, which equals the foreground cluster's weight. The task is to binarize the image: pick an intensity threshold so pixels above it are foreground and below it are background. A fixed threshold of 128 is the naive default; Otsu's method instead scans every threshold and picks the one that maximizes the between-class variance, which lands in the valley between the two histogram peaks. Here both peaks sit below 128, so a fixed 128 puts almost everything in background and the object nearly disappears, while Otsu recovers it. fixed_threshold is the naive default to compare against.
